title: Provably Correct Code Generation: Neuro-Symbolic Synthesis with Proof-Carrying Guarantees
background:
Large language models (LLMs) have rapidly advanced automated code synthesis, with systems such as Codex-derived assistants achieving 70-90% pass@1 on HumanEval-style benchmarks [1]. However, statistical correctness on test suites does not constitute formal correctness: recent audits show that 23-41% of LLM-generated functions accepted by unit tests contain latent specification violations, off-by-one errors, or unsafe memory patterns when subjected to symbolic execution [2]. This gap is unacceptable for safety-critical domains (avionics, medical devices, cryptographic libraries, smart contracts) where post-hoc bug discovery is prohibitively expensive. Concurrently, interactive theorem provers (Lean 4, Coq, Isabelle/HOL, Dafny, F*) and SMT-backed verifiers have matured, and recent work demonstrates that LLMs can draft proof sketches that close a non-trivial fraction of obligations [3][4]. Neuro-symbolic synthesis frameworks have begun coupling LLM proposers with symbolic verifiers in generate-and-check loops, yielding measurable gains on small benchmarks [5].

Despite this progress, three open gaps remain. First, specification acquisition is a bottleneck: developers rarely provide machine-checkable contracts, and inferring them from natural language is unreliable, with hallucinated invariants producing vacuous proofs [3]. Second, current pipelines treat verification as an external oracle, leading to exponential blowup in repair iterations and no principled mechanism for the LLM to learn from proof failures at scale [5]. Third, generated artifacts lack portable, independently checkable evidence: there is no standard for proof-carrying code (PCC) at the granularity and scale modern LLM synthesis demands, leaving downstream consumers to re-verify or trust blindly [6]. Closing these gaps requires tightly integrated training, decoding, and certificate-emission machinery that has not yet been demonstrated end-to-end.
challenges: Automatically eliciting and refining machine-checkable formal specifications (pre/postconditions, loop invariants, separation-logic assertions) from ambiguous natural-language intent without introducing under- or over-specified contracts that admit hallucinated proofs

Designing verification-aware decoding and training objectives (e.g., proof-conditioned RL, constrained beam search over typed ASTs) that propagate SMT/ITP feedback into the LLM's generative distribution rather than treating the verifier as a black-box rejection sampler

Scaling neuro-symbolic synthesis beyond single-function benchmarks to multi-file, stateful systems with heap-manipulating code, concurrency, and cross-module invariants while keeping proof obligations tractable for SMT solvers

Defining a compact, language-agnostic proof-carrying-code format and trusted minimal checker that allows third parties to validate LLM-generated artifacts in milliseconds without re-running the full synthesis or proof search

Establishing rigorous evaluation methodology and benchmarks that distinguish test-passing from formally verified code across realistic domains (cryptographic primitives, OS kernels, smart contracts) and quantify residual trust in the toolchain itself
